newsitem.title: INDIA: Marubeni says in iron ore deal in India.
newsitem.headline: Marubeni says in iron ore deal in India.

text.p: Japanese trading company Marubeni Corp said on Monday it was forming a joint venture with India's Sociedade de Fomento Industrial Ltd (FOMENTO) to develop new iron ore mines in the southern Indian state of Karnataka.

Marubeni and FOMENTO said in a joint statement that the 50/50 joint venture would build an offshore berth 10 km (six miles) off the coast of Goa state for the export of iron ores. The total project cost is about $110 million, it said.

The statement said Marubeni and FOMENTO had already made a preliminary feasibility study, and on Monday the companies agreed to conduct a detailed feasibility study by establishing a 50/50 joint venture called FOMAR Ltd.

The new mines in the Bellary-Hospet area of Karnataka will produce about 1.5 million tonnes of iron ore each year. The ore will be marketed through Marubeni in Japan as well as elsewhere in Asia and the Middle East, it said.
It said the offshore stockyard and berth, or OSB, will be made of concrete caissons measuring 200 metres (220 yards) in length and 45 metres (50 yards) in width.
The OSB will be able to accommodate vessels of up to 200,000 dead weight tonnage (DWT), the statement said. About 450,000 tonnes of bulk materials will be able to be stocked there, it said.
The statement said it would be the first time that concrete caissons had been used for iron ore loading facilities.
The OSB will also be used for imports of coal for steel and power plants. The firms expect the OSB to be able to handle about four million tonnes of iron ores and coal each year.
The detailed feasibility study will be finished by May 1997 and construction will start in June 1997, with a target for commissioning of October 1999, the statement said.
